title: Add docstrings to in-place functions with an out-of-place equivalent
body: Hi! I realized that with the release of 2.13, many new links started appearing on the left-side navigation bar of the documentation. A few examples: - torch.abs_() (and every in-place operation; before that they were all missing I think). - torch.slice_copy() (and every function suffixed by _copy, again I think all were missing in the 2.12 version of the docs). If I understand correctly, there was a bug that made them not appear, that was fixed in #178410. But now another problem surfaces: some of those functions don't have a docstring in Python so the built documentation page just contains the function's name. Also, when running e.g. `help(torch.abs_)` in python, only the function name appears. This PR focuses on adding the missing docstrings for in-place torch functions that have an out-of-place version (torch.abs_, torch.acos_, etc). It uses the same pattern as Tensor in-place methods (like Tensor.abs_) which do have a docstring linking to the out-of-place function's docstring. There are many more missing docstrings (close to 400 if my script listing them is correct), but it's gonna be very hard to fix everything in a single PR, which is why I'm only fixing the in-place torch ops in this PR. Before: After: cc @svekars @sekyondaMeta @AlannaBurke
